theater: 科西嘉島東岸阿拉利亞外海

battle.name: 阿拉利亞海戰
battle.theater: 科西嘉島東岸阿拉利亞外海
battle.brief: 公元前540年，波斯王居魯士攻陷福卡亞，福卡亞人帶家眷西遷，與馬薩利亞人聯手在阿拉利亞外海迎戰伊楚里亞與迦太基聯合艦隊。希臘方以五十人座戰船的衝角破敵，卻折損近三分之二戰艦，隨即撤出科西嘉。卡面亞述長弓是兩軍甲板弓兵共用的短弓，在登艦纏鬥中壓制對方水手。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 阿拉利亞海戰是公元前540年前後在科西嘉島東岸外海打的一場海戰，交戰一方是希臘人，另一方是伊楚里亞（伊特魯里亞）與迦太基的聯合艦隊。希臘方的主體是福卡亞人：公元前546年波斯王居魯士攻陷福卡亞城之後，這支住在安納托利亞西岸的伊奧尼亞海上族群把家眷、貨物和艦隊一併帶往西方，先落腳於自己建立的殖民地馬薩利亞（今馬賽），再以科西嘉島東岸的阿利亞為基地重建生活。與他們並肩作戰的馬薩利亞人本身就是福卡亞人建的殖民城，造船與划槳的傳統同源；島上的原住民與薩丁尼亞方面的盟友也被捲進戰局，後來在史家筆下成了最先崩潰的一翼。希臘方的組織形態是典型的城邦海軍：戰船由購船的公民階層自備並湊齊槳手，每條船上有划槳的槳手、操舵的人手、備著圓盾與短矛的登艦重裝步兵，以及在甲板射擊的弓箭手；決策由公民議會與各船船主共同作出，沒有留下一位可以指名的全軍統帥。聯軍方則是伊楚里亞與迦太基的海上聯盟。伊楚里亞人來自義大利半島中部，掌控鐵、銅與琥珀資源，靠一支數量可觀的艦隊守住第勒尼安海；迦太基是腓尼基城邦在北非的殖民主權，控制著西西里、薩丁尼亞與伊比利亞沿岸的商站網。兩家在商路上既競爭又合作，因此能在科西嘉外海組成遠比任何一方單獨力量為強的聯合艦隊。史料沒有留下聯軍的指揮結構，只能確定其戰術單位同樣是划槳戰船與登艦步兵的組合，而聯軍的戰略目標不是全殲，而是把這批帶著人口與財富的希臘殖民者從科西嘉趕走，切斷他們通往西班牙銀錫產區的航路。
countriesEn: The Battle of Alalia was a naval engagement fought off the eastern shore of Corsica around 540 BC, between a Greek fleet and an allied fleet of Tyrrhenians (Etruscans) and Carthaginians. The Greek side was centred on the Phocaeans, the seafaring Ionian people of Phocaea on the western Anatolian coast: after Cyrus the Great took Phocaea in 546 BC, they carried their households, their goods and their ships westward, first to their own colony of Massalia (modern Marseille) and then to Alalia on Corsica, where they tried to rebuild their life. Massaliots fought alongside them, and Massalia itself was a Phocaean foundation, so the shipbuilding and rowing traditions on the two sides were the same. Islanders and allies from Sardinia were drawn into the fighting and, in the pages of the historians, were the wing that broke first. The Greek organisation was that of the typical civic navy: the ships were owned and manned by the citizen class, each hull carrying rowers, helmsmen working two steering oars, hoplite marines equipped with a round shield and a short spear, and deck archers; decisions rested with a council of citizens and the ship-owning households, and no single commander is named for the battle itself. The other side was a maritime coalition of Etruscans and Carthaginians. The Etruscans of central Italy controlled iron, copper and amber and kept a sizeable fleet to guard the Tyrrhenian Sea; Carthage was the Phoenician colonial power in North Africa, holding a network of trading posts in Sicily, Sardinia and Iberia. The two were rivals and partners in trade at once, which is exactly why they could assemble off Corsica a combined fleet far stronger than either could have produced alone. The sources leave the allied command structure unrecorded; what can be established is that their tactical units were also combinations of rowing vessels and boarding infantry, and that the strategic purpose of the coalition was not annihilation but the removal of these Greek colonists, newly arrived with their population and wealth, from Corsica, and the cutting of their route to the silver and tin of Iberia.
people: 這場戰爭留下的人名不多，但每個名字都標出它的一環。第一個是波斯王居魯士大帝：公元前546年他先滅呂底亞，再逐一收拾伊奧尼亞各城，福卡亞是其中最早屈服的一座。正是這場征服把福卡亞的市民推上船，把一整座城的資產與人口搬進西方，間接製造了阿拉利亞海戰的交戰雙方。希臘方面最常被引用的名字是赫爾莫革涅斯（Hermogenes）：在希羅多德筆下，他是率領船隊離開被圍福卡亞的人；城破之後，他對著自己人讚賞敵城裡的酒太甜，反而讓波斯人相信這些守城的希臘人不是懦夫。這段插曲常被用來說明福卡亞人向西遷徙時的士氣，但海戰本身的指揮者，希羅多德並未點名，只說「福卡亞人打了勝仗」。另一位必須提到的開創者是普羅提斯（Protis）：約公元前600年，他帶領福卡亞人建立了馬薩利亞，那座城日後在海戰中扮演聯軍的角色，也是最終吸收了阿利亞難民的所在。海戰的另一翼是薩丁尼亞與科西嘉的舊居民，以及伊楚里亞、迦太基各城的船主；他們的指揮人沒有被記錄下來，但他們是這場戰役傷亡最重的一方。史料的編纂者希羅多德本人（約公元前484至前425年）在《歷史》第一卷記下了這場戰役，他說雙方都大量損毀了船隻，而薩丁尼亞人承受了最慘重的損失；後世的地理學家斯特拉波則補記了海戰之後福卡亞人遷往義大利南部建立埃萊亞（Elea，即後來的維利亞）的結局。從此以後，這場戰役還不斷被後世的航海史、殖民史與兵器史拿來引用，成為研究西地中海早期海戰與弓兵編制的標準案例。
peopleEn: Few names survive from this war, but each one marks a link in the chain. The first is Cyrus the Great: in 546 BC he destroyed Lydia and then worked through the Ionian cities one by one, and Phocaea was among the earliest to submit. That conquest is precisely what put the Phocaeans aboard their ships, carrying the assets and the population of an entire city westward, and so it manufactured the two opposing sides of the Battle of Alalia. The name most often attached to the Greek side is Hermogenes: in Herodotus he is the man who led the fleet out of besieged Phocaea, and after the city fell he praised to his companions the wine found in the enemy town as being too sweet, which persuaded the Persians that the defenders had not been cowards. The episode is often used to describe the morale of the Phocaeans on their western migration, but Herodotus names no commander of the sea battle itself, saying only that the Phocaeans won. Another figure who must be mentioned is the founder Protis: around 600 BC he led the Phocaeans to establish Massalia, the city that would later fight as an ally in the battle and would finally absorb the refugees from Alalia. On the other wing stand the older inhabitants of Sardinia and Corsica, together with the ship-owning houses of the Etruscan and Carthaginian cities; their commanders were never recorded, but they were the ones who suffered most. Herodotus himself, writing in the fifth century BC, preserved the account of the battle in the first book of his Histories, noting that both sides lost many ships and that the Sardinians bore the worst of it; the later geographer Strabo added the outcome that after the fight the Phocaeans moved to southern Italy and founded Elea, the city later known as Velia. Ever since, the battle has been cited again and again in histories of navigation, colonisation and arms, and it remains the standard case study for early naval warfare and for the organisation of archers in the western Mediterranean.
kits: 卡面上這張亞述長弓，來自亞述帝國覆亡之後仍在東方地中海與近東廣泛流傳的短型複合反曲弓：弓身以木為胎，外貼牛角片與筋腱，兩端反曲，拉力大而形狀緊湊。它的血統正是亞述弓兵在車上射擊時所用的那一種——亞述人就是靠弓與鐵的組合征服兩河流域；公元前612年尼尼微陷落之後，這種技術隨亞述的工匠與俘虜散入波斯、呂底亞以及希臘的伊奧尼亞海岸，福卡亞人是離亞述戰場最近的伊奧尼亞人之一。到公元前540年，短型複合反曲弓已是安納托利亞與波斯軍隊的標準弓式，迦太基的腓尼基步兵與伊楚里亞的登艦兵所用的短弓，也出自同一技術圈。在阿拉利亞海戰的編制裡，這張弓的位置是「船上的遠射臂」：五十人座戰船吃水淺、舷側低，銅包衝角可以撞裂敵船，卻難以單靠撞擊造成大量傷亡，真正決定登艦勝負的是登上敵船甲板的步兵；因此每條希臘船在槳手之上都編有弓箭手，用途是壓制敵方甲板、掩護掛鉤與搭梯，同時避免在己方即將接舷時誤傷自己人。希臘方面的近戰裝備以重裝步兵的圓盾（aspis）配合科林斯式青銅頭盔最為通行，頭盔的全覆面開眼設計要求整套隊形緊密，否則視線與號令都會失靈，兵種上再配短矛。遠征殖民的船隊裡攜帶大量箱櫃、炊具、水桶、繩索與備用槳，並備有裝滿陶罐的酒與糧食；對岸的伊楚里亞與迦太基則以自己的船隊載運步兵、投槍與標槍，準備以接舷纏鬥取勝。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card comes from the short composite recurve bow that kept circulating through the eastern Mediterranean and the Near East long after the Assyrian empire itself had gone: a wooden core faced with horn plates and sinew, recurving at both tips, short but of high draw weight. Its ancestry is exactly the bow the Assyrian archers used while shooting from their chariots, and it was the combination of bow and iron that carried the Assyrians through the Mesopotamian river valleys. After Nineveh fell in 612 BC, the technique spread with Assyrian craftsmen and prisoners into Persia, Lydia and the Ionian coast of Greece, and the Phocaeans were among the Ionians closest to the old Assyrian stamping ground. By 540 BC the short composite recurve was the standard bow of the Anatolian and Persian armies, and the short bows carried by the Phoenician soldiers of Carthage and the boarding infantry of the Etruscans came out of the same technological circle. In the order of battle at Alalia this bow occupied the place of the long-range arm carried aboard: the fifty-oared ship drew little water and presented a low flank, so the bronze-sheathed ram could split a hull but could not by itself produce the mass of casualties that decides a boarding action, and what really decided it was the infantry who got onto the enemy's deck. Every Greek ship therefore carried archers above the rowing level, whose task was to sweep the enemy deck, cover the grappling hooks and the boarding ladders, and above all to avoid shooting their own men in the moment their hulls came alongside. Greek close combat gear centred on the round shield of the hoplite (aspis) and the Corinthian bronze helmet, whose fully enclosing face opening demanded a tight formation if the men were to see and to hear orders, and the infantry also carried short spears. The colonising fleets travelled with great quantities of chests, cooking gear, water barrels, rope and spare oars, and with jars of wine and grain aboard; on the other side, the Etruscan and Carthaginian hulls carried infantry with javelins and spears, ready to win by close grappling.
tactics: 海戰的戰術細節在現存史料裡只剩骨架，希羅多德只記了勝負與損失，但可以從當時的技術條件推知作戰樣貌。希臘方靠的是已經成熟的划槳戰船戰術：全隊以縱列前進，每條船對準前一條船的船尾，只在接敵的最後一段以銅包衝角斜撞敵艦舷側，這樣的撞擊角度才足以把敵船的槳折斷、把船板撬開；列陣之前全隊必須維持同速，所以旗令、號角，加上善於配速的領航員，都是關鍵。五十人座戰船吃水淺、轉向快，但吃水淺也意味著衝角容易滑過敵船的吃水線，因此常配合另一種手段：在衝角之前先用弓箭齊射，把敵方甲板清空，再由登艦步兵在掛鉤與搭梯固定後蜂湧而上。卡面這張亞述長弓，正是這一步的主要工具；它短、張力大，適合在船身顛簸的甲板上一箭一箭地壓制，而不必像長弓那樣需要寬闊的射界。相對地，聯軍的船更多，卻多屬於以登舷為主的戰法：靠數量與接舷膠著取勝，弓兵的作用是掩護跳板，衝角多為撞散而非擊沉。戰場在科西嘉東岸外海，季風方向決定了雙方的進場角度：希臘人自東南方由薩丁尼亞海面駛入，聯軍則由西北方北義大利與北非的基地趕來，聯軍多一天行軍，就多一天要在科西嘉岸邊等上一場硬仗的風險。戰後的形勢也說明：希臘人雖然在海上得勝，卻因折損過半、無力防守，必須放棄阿利亞，帶著剩餘船隊退往馬薩利亞或義大利本土的雷吉翁。
tacticsEn: Only the skeleton of the tactical picture survives in the sources: Herodotus records the result and the losses, and the rest can be reconstructed from the technical conditions of the age. The Greek side relied on rowing tactics that were already mature: the fleet advanced in a line, each ship keeping the stern of the ship ahead, and only in the final approach did the bronze-sheathed ram strike the enemy's flank obliquely, since only that angle was capable of snapping oars and prising planks apart. Before the line closed, the whole fleet had to hold the same speed, which made the flags, the trumpet calls and the skill of the helmsmen in judging the rhythm decisive. The fifty-oared ship drew little water and turned quickly, but for exactly that reason its ram could slip past the enemy's waterline, so it was combined with a second method: a volley of arrows first, to clear the enemy deck, and only then did the boarding troops swarm across once the grappling hooks and ladders had bitten. The Assyrian bow on the card was the principal tool of that first step; short and of high tension, it could be worked one arrow at a time on a pitching deck, without needing the wide field of fire a long bow demanded. The coalition, with more ships but tactics built around closing and boarding, relied on numbers and on grappling until the hulls were locked together; their archers covered the boarding bridges and their rams were meant to scatter rather than to sink. The battleground lay off the eastern shore of Corsica, and the direction of the seasonal winds shaped the approaches: the Greeks came in from the south-east across the Sardinian Sea, while the coalition came from the north-west out of northern Italy and North Africa, and every extra day on the road meant one more day of waiting off the Corsican coast for a hard engagement. The aftermath makes the point as well: although the Greeks won at sea, losing more than half their fleet left them unable to hold the island, and they had to abandon Alalia and withdraw with the surviving ships to Massalia or to Rhegion on the Italian mainland.
data: 能夠落在紙上的數字不多，但有幾個可用的刻度。年代：現存通行說法把阿拉利亞海戰放在公元前540年前後，跨度有人寫到前540至前535年；直接背景是波斯王居魯士於前546年攻陷福卡亞。艦隊規模：一般推定希臘方出動約六十艘五十人座戰船（每船四十八支槳、兩支舵），聯軍艦隊約為其兩倍、接近一百二十艘同型船。這個六十對一百二十的說法出自現代史家的重建，屬推算而非史籍明文，史料本身只說聯軍「船數更多」。損失：希羅多德記錄雙方都損失了大量船隻與人馬，希臘方折損約三分之二，存活船隻的衝角嚴重受損，因此無力再守阿利亞；薩丁尼亞與科西嘉方面承受了最慘重的失敗，聯軍方面的具體數字不詳。時間與距離：福卡亞人先退到希俄斯島，再南下渡海到科西嘉，按古式航路估算全程約八百至一千海里（合一千五百至一千八百公里），實際航線與停靠地點已無從考訂；戰役必須落在春末至秋季的通航季內，季風時令與長距離補給都限制著他們的選擇。年代的下限還可由後續事件反推：海戰之後不久，福卡亞人於前540年遷往義大利南部建立埃萊亞；科西嘉隨後落入伊楚里亞人手中，薩丁尼亞則留在迦太基控制之下。科西嘉島東岸的阿利亞（今阿萊里亞）在羅馬時期成為一個行政區中心，這座城的名字正是從早年的殖民地沿用而來。今日這片海面因這場戰役與同期的「薩丁尼亞海戰」而共用同一個名字。
dataEn: Few figures survive on paper, but several usable anchors do. Dating: the usual reckoning places the Battle of Alalia around 540 BC, with some authors stretching the range to 540-535 BC; the immediate background is Cyrus the capture of Phocaea in 546 BC. Fleet size: it is generally reconstructed that the Greeks put to sea about sixty fifty-oared ships, each with forty-eight oars and two steering oars, while the allied fleet was about twice as large, close to a hundred and twenty vessels of the same type. The figure of sixty against a hundred and twenty is a modern reconstruction rather than a figure stated in the sources, which say only that the allied fleet had more ships. Losses: Herodotus records heavy losses of ships and men on both sides, the Greeks losing about two-thirds of their fleet, the surviving ships with their rams badly damaged and therefore unable to hold Alalia; the Sardinian and Corsican side bore the most crushing defeat, and the coalition's own losses are unknown. Time and distance: the Phocaeans first withdrew to Chios and then sailed south to Corsica, the whole passage estimated at roughly eight hundred to a thousand nautical miles, or one thousand five hundred to one thousand eight hundred kilometres along the old routes, the actual line and the ports of call no longer recoverable; the engagement had to fall inside the sailing season from late spring to autumn, and both the seasonal winds and the long lines of supply constrained the choices. The lower end of the date can be read back from what follows: shortly after the battle, in 540 BC, the Phocaeans moved to southern Italy and founded Elea; Corsica then passed into Etruscan hands, while Sardinia remained with Carthage. Alalia on the east coast of Corsica, modern Aleria, later became a centre of Roman administration, and the name of the place was carried down from the earlier settlement. The stretch of water has since taken the name of the battle and of the contemporary engagement also called the Battle of the Sardinian Sea.
cause: 打起來的原因可以分成三層。最內一層是福卡亞自己的處境：公元前546年居魯士的大軍攻克福卡亞，本城是伊奧尼亞諸城中最先被波斯逼降的，它的公民不願接受波斯的統治，便把城市財產裝上船，選擇繼續當一個海上民族。第二層是西地中海的資源分配：伊楚里亞人靠中部義大利的鐵、銅與琥珀維持自己的艦隊和城邦聯盟，迦太基靠北非的物資與遍布西西里、薩丁尼亞、伊比利亞的商站維持霸權；而希臘人從公元前750年起在義大利南部與西西里建立的一整片「大希臘」，連同馬薩利亞、阿加泰、阿格里翁、羅得等西方殖民城，正一步一步把航線與商品收進自己口袋。福卡亞人還把手伸進西班牙，用馬薩利亞的商路去換高盧的河運貨源與西班牙的銀、錫，這直接碰到伊楚里亞與迦太基的兩條命脈。第三層是眼前的觸發：阿利亞早已是福卡亞人在島上的據點，海戰前五年，希臘船隊在科西嘉一帶屢次騷擾伊楚里亞與迦太基的商船，掠走大量西地中海的金屬與貨物；兩家感到，下一步對方就會進攻自己在北義大利與薩丁尼亞的據點。於是約在公元前540年，兩方組成聯合艦隊撲向阿利亞外海，要一次解決這個不斷膨脹的希臘前哨。戰爭的深層原因是殖民與貿易的碰撞，而導火線是福卡亞的流亡人口帶著艦隊和財富登上了科西嘉的海岸。
causeEn: The reasons for the fight fall into three layers. The innermost is the situation of Phocaea itself: in 546 BC the army of Cyrus took the city, and Phocaea was the first of the Ionian cities to be forced to submit to Persia. Its citizens would not accept Persian rule, so they loaded the wealth of the city onto their ships and chose to remain a seafaring people. The second layer is the distribution of resources in the western Mediterranean. The Etruscans maintained their fleet and their league of city-states on the iron, copper and amber of central Italy; Carthage maintained its hegemony on the produce of North Africa and its chain of trading posts in Sicily, Sardinia and Iberia. Against that, the Hellenes had raised a whole Magna Graecia in southern Italy and Sicily from about 750 BC onward, together with the western foundations of Massalia, Agathe, Agathion, Rhode and others, and were step by step taking the sea lanes and the goods into their own hands. The Phocaeans reached further into Iberia, using the routes of Massalia to tap the river-borne trade of Gaul and the silver and tin of Spain, which struck directly at the two vital interests of the Etruscans and the Carthaginians. The third layer is the immediate trigger: Alalia had long been the Phocaean base on the island, and for the five years before the battle Greek warships had repeatedly harried Etruscan and Carthaginian merchantmen around Corsica, carrying off large quantities of western Mediterranean metal and goods. Both partners judged that the next step would be an assault on their own bases in northern Italy and Sardinia. So around 540 BC they combined their fleets and came at Alalia, intending to settle the matter with this swelling Greek outpost in one stroke. The deep cause was the collision of colonisation and trade; the trigger was a refugee population arriving on the Corsican coast with its fleet and its wealth.
impact: 這場海戰的結果，比它的過程更影響後世。希臘方在海上贏了，卻折損近三分之二戰艦、無力固守，於是放棄阿利亞：福卡亞人把剩餘的船、人和財產退向馬薩利亞，另有部分人渡海到義大利南部，在前540年前後建立了埃萊亞（Elea，日後稱維利亞），這座城後來以鹽業與醫學傳統聞名。科西嘉落入伊楚里亞人手中，薩丁尼亞留在迦太基手中；伊楚里亞人從此在西部海域失去主動，迦太基卻在西西里、薩丁尼亞與西班牙之間站穩，形成對希臘西進的長期牽制——直到前480年，迦太基仍在直布羅陀一線攔住希臘人通往西班牙的航路。馬薩利亞反而因為吸收了阿利亞的移民而壯大，成為西地中海最重要的希臘城之一，與阿加泰、埃姆波里翁、尼凱亞、安提波利斯組成一個面向高盧與伊比利亞的商業網。多年以後，正是馬薩利亞向羅馬求援，把羅馬拉進西地中海的列強競爭，羅馬與迦太基之間那場長達二十三年的第一次布匿戰爭由此發端。從兵器史的角度看，這是西地中海最早有記錄的大型海戰之一，它證明以銅包衝角划槈前進的戰船配合甲板弓兵，在地中海西部的實戰中仍然壓過以登舷為主的舊式海軍，也讓希臘式戰艦的戰術在此後數百年成為西地中海的標準。
impactEn: The consequences of this battle tell more about the future than its course did. The Greeks won at sea, but having lost close to two-thirds of their ships they could not hold the island, and so they gave up Alalia: the Phocaeans withdrew with the surviving ships, their people and their wealth towards Massalia, and part of them crossed to southern Italy, where around 540 BC they founded Elea, the city later called Velia, which became known for its salt pans and its school of medicine. Corsica passed to the Etruscans and Sardinia stayed with Carthage; the Etruscans from then on lost the initiative in the western sea, while Carthage consolidated its position between Sicily, Sardinia and Iberia and held the Greek advance in check for a long time, still shutting the Greek route to Spain at the Strait of Gibraltar as late as 480 BC. Massalia, by contrast, grew stronger precisely because it took in the refugees of Alalia, and became one of the most important Greek cities of the western Mediterranean, forming with Agathe, Emporion, Nikaia and Antipolis a commercial network aimed at Gaul and Iberia. Years later it was Massalia that called on Rome for help, pulling Rome into the struggle of the western Mediterranean powers, and from there began the First Punic War between Rome and Carthage, which would run for twenty-three years. From the point of view of the history of arms, this was among the earliest large naval battles recorded in the western Mediterranean. It showed that a rowing warship with a bronze-sheathed ram, supported by archers on the deck, still beat the older style of fleet built around boarding in the actual fighting of the western sea, and it made Greek ship tactics the standard in the western Mediterranean for centuries afterwards.
result: 要給這場海戰下結論，最貼切的說法是希羅多德借用的那個詞語：「卡德米亞式的勝利」——用自己的一部分毀滅去換對手的毀滅。海上層面，結果是清楚的：福卡亞人與馬薩利亞人的艦隊在阿拉利亞外海擊潰了伊楚里亞與迦太基的聯合艦隊，聯軍通往西西里、薩丁尼亞與西班牙的商路一度被打斷，島上的薩丁尼亞與科西嘉盟友遭到殘滅性打擊；希臘人一度控制阿利亞，可以說是「贏了這場海戰」。但戰略層面，結果同樣是清楚的：希臘方損失約三分之二的船，衝角受損，再無力防守島上基地；聯軍只需要再來一次，並不需要立刻再來。福卡亞人隨即撤出科西嘉，退往馬薩利亞與義大利，前540年建立埃萊亞；伊楚里亞人重新掌握科西嘉，迦太基保住薩丁尼亞。從長期的棋盤看，這一仗讓聯盟這一邊保住了西地中海的西半部，讓馬薩利亞單獨承擔了西方希臘世界的門戶角色，也讓希臘人第一次在西地中海見識到「海軍優勢不等於殖民地安全」。戰役的實際遺產因此是雙向的：西方希臘殖民的地理版圖往高盧方向推進，迦太基與伊楚里亞的海上同盟卻在這次勝負之後綁得更緊，最終把整個西地中海變成三方角力的舞台。傳說中被俘的希臘水手在伊楚里亞人的城邦卡雷被石頭砸死，在迦太基則被賣為奴隸；這段說法出自後世記載，未經當時文件的核對，但可以確定的是，俘虜的待遇是當時地中海世界裡最尖銳的爭議之一。
resultEn: For a verdict on this battle, the most exact phrase is the one Herodotus borrowed: a Cadmean victory, won by exchanging part of one's own destruction for the destruction of the enemy. At sea the result is plain. The fleet of the Phocaeans and Massaliots broke the allied Tyrrhenian-Carthaginian fleet off Alalia; the coalition's trade routes towards Sicily, Sardinia and Iberia were cut for a time; and the Sardinian and Corsican allies of the coalition were crushed. For a while the Greeks held Alalia, and in that sense they won the battle. But at the strategic level the result is just as plain: the Greeks had lost about two-thirds of their ships, their rams were damaged, and they could no longer defend a base on the island. The coalition only had to come once more; it did not have to come immediately. The Phocaeans left Corsica and withdrew to Massalia and to Italy, founding Elea in 540 BC; the Etruscans took Corsica back and Carthage kept Sardinia. On the long board, the battle left the coalition holding the western half of the western Mediterranean, left Massalia alone to carry the burden of being the gateway of the Hellenic west, and taught the Greeks in the western Mediterranean for the first time that naval superiority does not guarantee the safety of a colony. The legacy of the engagement is therefore two-sided: the geography of Greek colonisation in the west pushed forward towards Gaul, while the maritime partnership between Carthage and the Etruscans was tightened by the outcome and the whole western Mediterranean became the stage for a three-cornered contest. Legend has it that Greek prisoners were stoned to death at the Etruscan city of Caere and sold into slavery at Carthage; the story comes down from later accounts without confirmation from contemporary documents, but what can be certain is that the treatment of prisoners was among the sharpest controversies of the ancient Mediterranean.
